context: Current closing price of Berkshire Hathaway B (BRK-B): $488.53 USD as of 2026-07-16.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term bias anchored around the prevailing price level, with gentle upward drift over longer horizons. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of roughly 489–490 suggests I expected minimal movement from the most recent close, consistent with typical daily volatility in a large-cap equity index like the S&P 500 ETF or a comparable instrument trading near that level. The slight upward tilt at one week and one month reflects a baseline assumption that equity markets carry a small positive drift over time, compounded by the absence of any immediately obvious catalyst for a sharp sell-off at the time of the forecast.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to historical realized volatility at each horizon. At one day, a 19-point range captures roughly plus or minus one standard deviation of typical daily moves. As the horizon extends to one week and one month, the intervals widen substantially — from a 38-point range at one week to a 75-point range at one month — reflecting how uncertainty compounds with time. This scaling is broadly consistent with a random-walk assumption where uncertainty grows with the square root of time. The asymmetry in the month-ahead interval is modest, reflecting that equity distributions tend to have slightly fat downside tails, though I didn't build in extreme skew.

The primary upside risks that could push outcomes above my stated intervals include a stronger-than-expected macroeconomic data release, a dovish pivot or surprise rate cut signal from central banks, or a resolution of geopolitical tensions that had been weighing on sentiment. On the downside, the most significant tail risks include a credit event or liquidity stress in financial markets, an unexpected inflation surge that re-prices rate expectations sharply higher, or an escalation in geopolitical conflict. These kinds of event-driven outcomes are by their nature difficult to assign precise probabilities to and represent the main source of potential interval violations. Over the one-month horizon in particular, the range of plausible macro outcomes is wide enough that I would treat the stated 90% interval with genuine humility — real-world fat tails mean the true coverage of such intervals is often lower than stated.
